title: Make STH computation event-driven via ChainPubSub

story.i_want_to: wire ComputeSthWorker to listen to AuditChain.PubSub (ChainPubSub) broadcasts when new entries are appended, and enqueue per-tenant STH jobs on-demand with bounded debouncing instead of running an all-tenants poll every minute
story.so_that: idle tenants with no new activity do not cost a job and two database queries per minute, and active tenants see faster STH computation (event-driven, no 60s latency waiting for the next cron tick)

rationale: The current all-tenants cron polls every 60s and fans out N single-row inserts (now chunked). This wastes ~N jobs/min on idle tenants and causes a thundering herd at each `:00` tick. ChainPubSub already broadcasts whenever an entry is appended (US-26.5.1); subscribing to that broadcast and enqueueing on-demand is event-driven with no polling waste. A low-frequency safety sweep (e.g., every 15 min) remains as a backstop for edge cases (broadcast miss, subscriber crash).

acceptance_criteria.description: ComputeSthWorker adds a new perform/1 clause: perform(%Oban.Job{args: %{"mode" => "on_demand", "tenant_id" => tenant_id}}) that computes STH for a single tenant
ComputeSthWorker retains the all_tenants mode (args: %{"mode" => "all_tenants"}) but reduces its frequency from every 60 seconds to every 900 seconds (15 minutes), as a safety sweep only
A new Loopctl.AuditChain.PubSub.SubscriberWorker subscribes to ChainPubSub entry broadcasts and enqueues a uniquely-debounced ComputeSthWorker job (mode: on_demand) for each tenant
On-demand jobs use unique: [fields: [:worker, :args], period: 10] to debounce multiple entries appended within 10 seconds for the same tenant to a single STH computation
The SubscriberWorker is started as a named, supervised process (or LiveView subscription, if using Loopctl's web layer) on application startup
Tests verify that appending an entry triggers an on_demand STH job and that the job computes the STH correctly

test_cases.name: Appending an entry enqueues an on_demand STH job
steps: Append a new entry to the tenant's chain
Wait briefly for the PubSub broadcast and subscriber processing
Check Oban.Job table for a ComputeSthWorker job with mode=on_demand and tenant_id
expected_results: Job has correct tenant_id and mode

test_cases.name: Multiple entries within 10 seconds debounce to one STH job
steps: Append 5 entries to the tenant's chain in rapid succession (within 5 seconds)
Wait for PubSub broadcasts and subscriber processing
Count the on_demand STH jobs enqueued for that tenant

test_cases.name: All-tenants sweep still works every 15 minutes
steps: Advance time by 15 minutes (mock time or real wait if acceptable)
Check for all_tenants mode job in Oban
expected_results: all_tenants job is enqueued at the 15-minute mark

test_cases.name: on_demand mode performs correctly
preconditions: A tenant exists with an entry
steps: Create an on_demand Oban.Job manually with correct args
Fetch the STH for that tenant
expected_results: STH is computed and stored correctly

notes: The SubscriberWorker needs to be kept alive across application restarts; use a supervised GenServer or Phoenix.PubSub subscription. If using a GenServer, keep it simple: just listen and enqueue jobs. No business logic in the subscriber, to minimize crash surface. Test with both real PubSub broadcasts and mocked broadcasts (Mox).
